title: NexusOps

listing.shortDescription: A multi-agent operations platform that triages support, qualifies sales leads and governs high-risk actions across omnichannel inbound traffic — with human sign-off on everything that matters.
listing.fullDescription: Inbound customer operations were drowning in manual work: tickets routed by hand, sales inquiries sitting in inboxes, and production incidents escalating slowly across fragmented tools. We built a four-agent orchestration platform — triage, technical support, BANT sales qualification and governance — that classifies every inbound event semantically, resolves what it safely can, and pauses anything risky in a human approval queue with full audit trail.

features.title: Four-agent DAG orchestration
features.description: Aegis, Vanguard, Meridian and Apex hand off execution state across a verified directed acyclic graph.

features.title: Semantic triage & routing
features.description: Intent, confidence, sentiment and entity extraction decide the branch before any tool runs.

features.title: Human-in-the-loop gates
features.description: Low confidence, large concessions and production changes pause in an operator approval queue.

features.title: Self-healing integration engine
features.description: Exponential backoff retries and circuit breakers recover from rate limits and timeouts automatically.

features.title: BANT sales qualification
features.description: Budget, authority, need and timeline scored with live ARR sizing and CRM pipeline provisioning.

features.title: Tamper-evident audit trail
features.description: Every prompt, tool invocation, payload change and operator decision recorded with resource IDs.

challenge.summary: Manual triage, fragmented tools and unenforced governance meant slow escalations, unattended leads and silent integration failures for a high-SLA enterprise support operation.

points.title: Context scattered across silos
points.description: Zendesk, HubSpot, internal wikis and Slack each held part of the customer picture, copied by hand.

points.title: Slow escalation
points.description: Standard bots either hallucinated actions or failed on anything beyond keyword matching.

points.title: No structured authorization
points.description: Refunds, patches and custom SLA terms had no formal approval mechanism before execution.

points.title: Silent integration failures
points.description: Rate limits and webhook drops failed workflows silently, dropping customer interactions.

solution.summary: A deterministic multi-agent pipeline where every inbound event is classified semantically, resolved autonomously within hard safety boundaries, and paused for human sign-off the moment a boundary is approached.

points.title: Verified DAG execution
points.description: A serialized step executor with promise barriers prevents race conditions between concurrent agents.

points.title: Dual-tier reasoning
points.description: Claude Code structured inference with a deterministic local classifier as a crash-free fallback.

points.title: Hard HITL safety gates
points.description: Confidence below 0.80, discounts above $1,000 and Sev-1 incidents pause until operator sign-off.

points.title: Resilient connector layer
points.description: Three exponential-backoff retries per connector before a circuit breaker trips and alerts.

points.title: Full observability
points.description: Live DAG topology, step-level telemetry traces and an immutable audit log for every action.

objectives: Route every inbound event by semantic intent instead of manual triage
Qualify sales leads with BANT scoring and live ARR sizing
Enforce human sign-off on every high-risk autonomous action
Survive connector failures with retry, backoff and circuit breaking
Keep a tamper-evident audit trail of every agent action

closing.clientOverview: An enterprise B2B SaaS platform serving high-stakes customers across Standard, Growth and Enterprise tiers with guaranteed SLAs. Support and sales engineering teams were overwhelmed by manual ticket routing and lead qualification, while every external integration failure silently dropped customer interactions until an engineer manually replayed them.
closing.conclusion: NexusOps now runs every inbound event through a deterministic four-agent DAG: Aegis routes semantically, Vanguard resolves technical issues against the knowledge base, Meridian qualifies and sizes sales leads into the CRM pipeline, and Apex enforces governance — pausing any action with low confidence or high risk in a human approval queue. Every tool call is logged, every failure retries with exponential backoff, and the platform can be fault-tested live from its own connector hub.
